learning_goal: Name the three parts of a blastocyst on a cut drawing, say what each becomes, explain how the cavity is made and why the embryo must hatch before it can implant, and date days five to six correctly.

structures.name: Zona pellucida — stretched, thinned, then breached
structures.label: Zona pellucida — stretched, thinned, then breached
structures.narration: The blastocyst cannot implant while the zona is around it, because the zona is exactly what has been preventing attachment for four days. On about day five the expanding cavity thins the shell and trophoblast enzymes help break it, and the blastocyst squeezes out. Hatching must come before implantation, always in that order. A zona too tough to breach is one cause of repeated failure after embryo transfer, which is why a laboratory sometimes thins it artificially.

structures.name: Trophectoderm — the morula's outer layer, before polar and mural exist
structures.label: Trophectoderm — the outer layer of the morula
structures.narration: Before there is a cavity there is one outer layer, and it has one name. The morula's outer cells have already committed to becoming trophoblast, but polar and mural are positional labels — they mean the part over the inner cell mass and the part away from it — and until the cavity pushes the mass to one end there is no over and no away. The split into polar and mural is something the cavity does, not something the cells have done yet.
structures.narration_from: WRITTEN IN ROUND 3, 2026-10-02, and the only narration in this scene that is not carried over from the SVG version. It exists because the review's R2 found beat 1 drawing the polar/mural distinction on a solid morula, at the equator — a latitude the real boundary never occupies — and the fix is to draw one layer there and say why it is one. It makes the same point beat 5 makes from the other end, and it is deliberately about the LABELS rather than about the cells: the commitment is early, the names are not.

structures.name: Mural trophoblast — the thin wall away from the mass
structures.label: Mural trophoblast — the thin wall away from the mass
structures.narration: The single flattened layer around the outside, away from the inner cell mass — and it is the half of the trophoblast that does NOT invade. It is the thinner of the two for the whole of this scene, and it is what the expanding fluid presses against. It becomes the chorion laeve, the smooth chorion, which regresses rather than forming placenta; the villous placenta forms over the opposite pole, where the mass sits. Like all trophoblast it contributes nothing to the fetus. At the implantation site — which is the polar surface, not this one — the trophoblast splits into an inner cytotrophoblast, which keeps dividing, and an outer syncytiotrophoblast, which fuses into one multinucleate mass and does the invading. A tumour of this tissue is a hydatidiform mole — placenta without an embryo, which is why it produces enormous amounts of hCG and no fetal parts.

structures.name: Inner cell mass (embryoblast)
structures.label: Inner cell mass (embryoblast)
structures.narration: A knot of cells at one end, inside the cavity. Everything in the fetus comes from here, and it also makes the amnion and the yolk sac. Within days it will split into epiblast and hypoblast to form the bilaminar disc. It is pluripotent, not totipotent — it can make any tissue of the body but can no longer make a placenta, and that distinction is the exam point. Embryonic stem cell lines are derived from it.

structures.name: Blastocyst cavity (blastocoele) — pumped fluid
structures.label: Blastocyst cavity (blastocoele) — pumped fluid
structures.narration: The fluid space that turns a solid morula into a hollow blastocyst. It is what pushes the inner cell mass off-centre, and its expansion is what stretches and thins the zona until the embryo can escape. Grading in a laboratory is largely a judgement about how far this cavity has expanded. By the time the embryo hatches it is half again the width of the morula that entered the uterus, and not one cell has grown to do it — the whole increase is pumped fluid.

views.title: How the cavity is made — it is pumped, not left behind

ops.kind: pumps sodium inward through a sealed sheet, and water follows
its expansion is what pushes the mass to one end

views.narration:
The cavity is not a gap that appears; it is pumped. The outer cells are sealed to one another by tight junctions and drive sodium inward with a sodium-potassium ATPase. Water follows through aquaporins and cannot leak back out through the seal, so it accumulates in one space and inflates it. The morula becomes a blastocyst at about day five, and the growing cavity pushes the inner cell mass to one end.

The outer cells are sealed together by tight junctions and pump sodium inward with a sodium-potassium ATPase on their inner face. Water follows the salt through aquaporins, and because the seal will not let it leak back out, it collects in one growing space. That is cavitation, and it is pure physics — an ion pump plus a watertight sheet.

views.title: Hatching must come first

ops.kind: stretched thin by the expanding cavity, and now breached

views.narration: For four days the zona pellucida has been stopping the embryo from sticking to anything. It now has to go. views.narration:
A step back in time, and it is deliberate: this beat stands at day five, BEFORE the attachment you have just seen. The zona is back because the embryo has not FINISHED hatching — it is thinned and already breached, and the blastocyst is still inside it — that is the order, and this is the stage the clinic works at.

Four practical points. Transferring at day five selects embryos that survived the genome handover, so fewer are replaced and fewer twins result. Genetic testing takes cells from the trophectoderm, which is safer and more representative than a day-three blastomere and does not touch the future fetus. The zona can be thinned artificially when hatching keeps failing. And where the blastocyst lands settles two diagnoses in advance: too low in the uterus is a placenta praevia, still in the tube is an ectopic pregnancy.

The blastocyst is where assisted reproduction now does most of its work. Transfer at day five selects the embryos that survived the genome handover, so fewer need to be replaced. Cells for genetic testing are taken from the trophectoderm rather than from the embryo itself, which is both safer and more representative than a day-three blastomere. The zona can be thinned to help hatching. And the two ways implantation goes wrong in position — too low, or never leaving the tube — are both decided in the next forty-eight hours.

deferred_beats.title: A later split shares more
deferred_beats.narration: Once a blastocyst has formed, only the inner cell mass can still split, and the trophoblast around it cannot be duplicated. So twins arising between days four and eight share one placenta and have two amnions, and that shared circulation is what makes twin-to-twin transfusion possible. A split between days eight and thirteen shares the amnion as well; later still and the twins are conjoined. The membranes on the scan date the split.
deferred_beats.also: Once the trophoblast is committed, a split can no longer duplicate it. An inner cell mass that divides between days four and eight gives twins with one placenta and two amnions — monochorionic, diamniotic — and that shared placenta is what allows twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome. A split between days eight and thirteen shares the amnion too, and a later one leaves them conjoined. Read the membranes backwards and they date the split.
deferred_beats.why_not_a_view: It needs geometry this model does not build: a SECOND inner cell mass inside one trophoblast, and then a third case sharing one amnion. The model solves a single mass against a single volume constraint, and a twin variant is a real build rather than a flag — the same reason the cleavage scene defers its own twinning beat. Both texts are kept whole. If a future round builds a twin variant, this is the beat it belongs to, and it wants the cut variants and a lateral camera.

deferred_beats.title: hCG and the corpus luteum
deferred_beats.narration: The syncytiotrophoblast starts secreting human chorionic gonadotropin almost as soon as it invades. hCG acts on the LH receptor of the corpus luteum and keeps it producing progesterone, so the endometrium is not shed and the period is missed. It is detectable in blood about eight days after fertilization. Every pregnancy test in every clinic is measuring a product of this cell layer, not of the embryo.
deferred_beats.why_not_a_view: Nothing in it has form at this scale, and the cell layer it is about — the syncytiotrophoblast — is a WEEK TWO differentiation that this scene's own gaps[] already places outside its scope. Its teaching reaches a student inside beat 9, whose narration (verbatim from the SVG version) carries the hCG sentences; this entry keeps the longer text so nothing is lost. A beat drawing a hormone would be a label on a frame already shown, which RENDER-STANDARD calls text.

deferred_beats.title: Implantation begins (day 6)
deferred_beats.narration: About day six the hatched blastocyst lies against the endometrium, sticks to it, and the syncytiotrophoblast begins to eat its way in. The usual site is the upper posterior wall of the uterus. A blastocyst that implants low sets up a placenta praevia; one that never reached the uterus implants in the tube. By the end of week one it is only partly embedded — full burial belongs to week two.

The full text is kept here because it is the best statement in the corpus of what day six is, and beat 9 carries the half of it this scene can show.

AXES. +y is the EMBRYONIC POLE and is NOT a body direction. The model is axisymmetric apart from its section function, has no chiral content and no mesh-anchored right/left pair, so per RENDER-STANDARD ("a declared axis is not a proved one, and a symmetric model cannot prove its own") no handedness claim is made anywhere, and no narration in this scene names a left or a right of the body. THE UTERUS IS NOT DRAWN, and what replaces it is a 260 µm patch of secretory endometrium at TRUE scale with two gland openings. At 10 µm per unit a uterus is 5,000 units across, so there is no honest single-scale frame holding both it and a 200 µm blastocyst. The cleavage scene met the same problem and answered it with a schematic tube at its own declared scale, because its subject was a journey; this scene's subject is in CONTACT with a wall, so a true-scale window on that wall is the honest picture and there is no scale break anywhere in this scene.

THE PUMP HAS NO GEOMETRY. Tight junctions, the sodium-potassium ATPase and the aquaporins are narration (beat 2, verbatim from the SVG scene) and are not drawn: at 10 µm they have no form and a drawn "junction" would be an invention. What the geometry carries is what they CAUSE — one growing space that cannot leak back out — and the growth and the cavity are the same quantity by construction, which acceptance row F asserts.

THE ZONA'S THINNING HERE IS MECHANICAL ONLY. Its own material volume is conserved while the expanding embryo stretches it, so the modelled thinning — 15.2 µm down to 9.3 µm by the breach, row Z — is a LOWER BOUND on the real thinning, which also has trophoblast lysins working on it. The narration names the enzymes; the geometry does not model them.

HATCHING HAS NO WAIST. A real blastocyst herniates out of its zona hourglass-shaped, over hours. This model has no shell mechanics, so the blastocyst stays centred and the breach opens from the abembryonic pole until the shell is gone. The alternative was tried and is geometrically impossible here, not merely harder: an expanded blastocyst (R = 9.2) is LARGER than its own unstretched zona (outer radius 7.72), so the moment the shell is allowed to relax it is entirely inside the embryo. The site of the breach is a composition choice — the pole with no mass behind it, so the escape does not draw over the subject — the teaching texts do not fix it, and nothing here claims it.

THE SHED ZONA IS NOT DRAWN after hatching, for the same reason: an intact sphere beside a blastocyst larger than itself is a geometric lie, and a crumpled remnant needs a crumple law this model does not have. The shell leaves CONTINUOUSLY as the breach opens, so no frame loses it between two frames, and row H measures that it goes.

NO CELL COUNTS ANYWHERE, which the SVG version already decided and this version keeps: published blastocyst counts vary too widely to be a fact a student should reproduce. Individual cells are not drawn either — the trophoblast is built as a LAYER whose thickness is the examinable property, not as a tessellation of cells. A student is examined on "a single flattened layer", which is a thickness, and beat 6 is the beat that shows it. If a future round wants cell outlines on the wall, that is new geometry and a new claim.

CYTOTROPHOBLAST AND SYNCYTIOTROPHOBLAST are named inside the trophoblast narration and are not built or given structures, because they are strictly a week-two differentiation. Unchanged from the SVG version's own gap, and still correct.

THIS SCENE STOPS AT APPOSITION. Beat 9 draws the blastocyst lying against the endometrium and measures the gap and which pole closes it. Adhesion, invasion, the lacunar stage and the bilaminar disc belong to "Implantation" and "Bilaminar embryonic disc" in the next topic and are NOT claimed in covers[]. HIGHLIGHT INTENSITY IS NOT INDEPENDENT OF THE STRUCTURE'S OWN COLOUR, AND THREE BEATS WERE CALIBRATED FOR IT WHILE THE REST WERE MEASURED AND LEFT. CHANGED: beat 2's blastocoele_cut 0.95 -> 0.35, beat 3's icm_cut 0.9 -> 0.40, beat 4's icm_cut 0.95 -> 0.40. The mass now reads (96,162,255) in beat 3 against the fluid's (137,247,255) — saturated tissue, pale space. THE GENERAL RULE THE CORPUS DOES NOT STATE: an emissive highlight is a fixed ADDITION, so the intensity that reads as a glow depends on what it is added to, and a scene that uses one number everywhere is calibrated for its darkest structure only.
